USER TURN 7

ASSISTANT TURN 7 (2 messages, last privileged)
[earlier] I’ll draw the exact current build path, startup path, and the missing-information point. The issue is not that startup cannot build files; it is that it cannot calculate the same cache key as `agent-vm build`. I’m using the TUI presentation guidance for the flow.
[last] ...[truncated]...
─────────────

```text
Authored image configuration
          │
          ▼
Build Docker image
          │
          ▼
Inspect actual Docker filesystem layers
          │
          │   produces rootfs identity: LAYER-123
          ▼
Calculate VM fingerprint from:

  build config
  + Agent VM version
  + Gondolin version
  + generated boot script
  + Docker rootfs identity: LAYER-123
          │
          ▼
fingerprint: ABC123
          │
          ├──► shared image
          │
          │    ~/.agent-vm/cache/vm-images/ABC123/
          │
          └──► deployment selection
               ~/.agent-vm/shravan-claw-xxxx/
                 cache/image-selections/gateway/hermes.json

               contents:
                 profile hermes uses fingerprint ABC123
```

The Docker rootfs identity is calculated in [build-command.ts](/Users/shravansunder/Documents/dev/project-dev/agent-vm.cache/packages/agent-vm/src/cli/build-command.ts:852).

─── Normal startup ───────────────────────────────────────────────────

```text
agent-vm controller start
          │
          ▼
Read deployment selection
          │
          ▼
hermes.json says fingerprint ABC123
          │
          ▼
Verify shared image ABC123 exists and is complete
          │
          ▼
Boot ABC123
```

This is fast. Startup does not build anything.

─── The problem case ─────────────────────────────────────────────────

Suppose the selection is missing:

```text
~/.agent-vm/shravan-claw-xxxx/
  cache/image-selections/gateway/hermes.json

  ✗ missing
```

Startup still has the authored recipe:

```text
build config
Agent VM version
Gondolin version
generated boot script
```

But it does not know:

```text
Docker rootfs identity: LAYER-123
```

Therefore it cannot reproduce the same fingerprint:

```text
agent-vm build knows:

  CONFIG + VERSIONS + BOOT SCRIPT + LAYER-123
                          │
                          ▼
                        ABC123


controller startup knows:

  CONFIG + VERSIONS + BOOT SCRIPT + ?????????
                          │
                          ▼
                 cannot prove ABC123
```

If startup simply ignores the missing value, it might calculate a different key and create a duplicate or incorrectly identified image.

─── The two clean choices ────────────────────────────────────────────

```text
CHOICE 1 — Require build first

agent-vm build
  ──► Docker build and inspection
  ──► shared image ABC123
  ──► selection hermes.json

controller start
  ──► reads selection
  ──► boots ABC123

selection missing
  ──► stop
  ──► “Run agent-vm build first”
```

Gain:

```text
one owner for building images
startup remains fast
fingerprint is always trustworthy
```

Cost:

```text
operator must run agent-vm build before controller start
```

```text
CHOICE 2 — Build during startup

controller start
  ──► Docker build
  ──► inspect Docker layers
  ──► calculate fingerprint
  ──► build Gondolin image
  ──► write selection
  ──► finally boot Gateway
```

Gain:

```text
startup repairs a missing selection automatically
```

Cost:

```text
controller startup now owns the entire build pipeline
startup can take minutes
startup requires Docker and build tooling
build failures become controller-start failures
two separate entrypoints own image building
```

─── My recommendation ────────────────────────────────────────────────

```text
agent-vm build             owns image construction
controller start           only verifies and boots the selection
missing/invalid selection  says “Run agent-vm build”
```

That gives us the clean final model:

```text
authored configuration
          │
          ▼
agent-vm build
          │
          ├──► shared immutable image
          │
          └──► deployment selection
                         │
                         ▼
                 controller start
                         │
                         ▼
                       boot
```

I recommend Choice 1: require `agent-vm build` first.
